chunks: Al-Ḥalabī narrated from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام:
Regarding the muhrim wearing a buttoned taylasan, he said: “Yes. In the Book of ʿAlī عليه السلام: ‘Do not wear a taylasan until you undo its buttons.’”
And he said: “That was only disliked out of fear that an ignorant person might fasten it upon himself; but as for the juristically knowledgeable one, there is no harm in his wearing it.”

key_terms.ٱلطَّيْلَسَانَ: a cloak or outer garment referred to in the ruling
key_terms.ٱلْجَاهِلُ: an ignorant person lacking knowledge of the ruling
key_terms.ٱلْفَقِيهُ: a knowledgeable jurist or one who understands the legal ruling
key_terms.ٱلْمُحْرِمِ: a person in the state of ihram for hajj or ʿumrah

ai.seo_question: Can a muhrim wear a buttoned taylasan during ihram?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning clothing worn in the state of ihram, specifically a buttoned taylasan. The Imam عليه السلام cites the Book of ʿAlī عليه السلام and explains that the dislike is precautionary, to prevent improper fastening by the ignorant, while a knowledgeable person may wear it without harm.
